question.worked_solution:
First, we write $5\,\frac{1}{3}$ as an improper fraction:

$$
5\,\frac{1}{3}=\frac{(5\times 3)+1}{3}=\frac{16}{3}
$$

We also write  $1\,\frac{1}{4}$ as an improper fraction:

$$
1\,\frac{1}{4}=\frac{(1\times 4)+1}{4}=\frac{5}{4}
$$

Now, we can multiply the two numbers. 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{16}{3}\times \frac{5}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

We can simplify this product by swapping the denominators:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{16}{3}\times \frac{5}{4} & =\frac{16}{4}\times \frac{5}{3} \\  & =4\times \frac{5}{3} \\  & =\frac{20}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we write the resulting improper fraction as a mixed number:

$$
\frac{20}{3}=6\,\text{R}2=6\,\frac{2}{3}
$$
